assessment: 2023 protocol Table 1 dietary management allows walnut oil among several oil choices within multimodal diabetes-mild cognitive impairment management; no cold-pressed specification, assigned walnut oil contrast, Parkinson population, or pain endpoint. Protocol not results.

Author Rosemary Gallagher is a name, not a herb; Methods and Results test auditory/visual cues on stationary cycling cadence in PD and older controls, not dietary rosemary or walking speed intervention. Prior gait-speed work is discussed as background.

Author Rosemary Joan Gowran is a name; arts-based music and movement protocol in community-dwelling older adults includes timed mobility and SPPB walking speed but no rosemary intervention or reported trial results.

Author Rosemary Babcock is a name; 68-year-old with olivopontocerebellar atrophy received amplitude-based physiotherapy, with preferred and maximal gait speed among outcomes, not ground rosemary. Original body not verified; PubMed abstract and institutional record accessed.
Methods describe visual and motor imagery training and record Starkstein Apathy Scale ratings. Jared Cherry is the lead author. The experiment did not assign a cherry-food exposure.

Laboratory NMR oxidation of supermarket walnut oil with added tocopherol at 40 or 70 C; pain and Parkinson disease are background discussion, not consumed oil or clinical pain outcome; pressing unverified.
Review discusses whole-walnut feeding in cisplatin-exposed mice and walnut leaf extract in diabetic neuropathy; neither establishes cold-pressed oil or Parkinson pain.

Review cites Raafat 2018 walnut oil and kernel extracts for diabetic mouse nociception. The original uses hexane Soxhlet oil, not cold-pressed, and is already catalogued; no human Parkinson pain comparison.

Review lists BRAVO NCT01901887 in ongoing studies: omega-3 smoothie vs fruit juice containing macadamia oil 1100 mg three times daily; depression and negative affect planned; not a pooled completed macadamia result, verified cold-press grade, or Parkinson cohort.
Young and older adults walked under virtual-reality optic-flow perturbations; Rosemary Blieszner is decision editor, not an ingested herb; no Parkinson rosemary intervention.
Cochrane review of physical rehabilitation in long-term care; Rosemary Campbell-Blair acknowledged for search help, not the plant; no rosemary food/gait comparison.
Systematic review of motion-analysis fall predictors in older adults; Rosemary Dubbeldam is an author, not an intervention with ground rosemary.
Scoping review of environmental factors in technology-assisted physical activity; Rosemary Dubbeldam is an author, not an ingested herb or Parkinson gait comparison.

Eleven people with Parkinson disease had 12 weeks of overground locomotor training, and walking speed increased p=.012; Rosemary Higgins is an author, not a rosemary dietary arm. Full paper remains access-limited.

Parkinson brain-fog review proposes rosemary-derived isolated carnosic acid based on preclinical mechanisms and says no clinical study published for that application; no ground rosemary or walking-speed result.

Review footnote calls an STW5 ingredient cumin in discussion of dyspepsia; original product composition identifies caraway fruit Carum carvi, not Cuminum cyminum. Neither the multiextract dyspepsia evidence nor general Parkinson dysphagia discussion measures toasted cumin swallowing.
